notes: Most disagreement was phase (before-course vs course-start vs general vs over-time for syllabus duties and institutional principles), resolved by two rules: syllabus-statement duties are course-start, and UNM's value statements are general. Type disagreements were mostly between neighbouring types (P83/P35 for redesign, P91/P18 and P15/P12 for permitted uses, P45/P24 for attribution, P36/P45 for plagiarism examples); each was resolved by re-reading the sentence and choosing the type whose definition the sentence states, with a fit_note when only partly. Where one coder used UNCOVERED, the unit was mapped to an existing type if the type's definition really fit (simulation for practice -> P14; reading before summarising -> P90; policy-status statements and AI-drafting footnotes -> P84) and kept UNCOVERED when it did not (right to explanation and redress; AI drafting of text for critique). Modality disagreements came from lists (informs vs must-not) and were set from the source verb. Alignment was done by overlapping source spans; three pairs that the automatic alignment crossed were re-paired by hand (values 5.1 list, the 'submit work you do not understand' sentence) and two single-sentence units that held two rules were kept as separate units. Units found by one coder: all kept except one generic trust sentence (coder A) and three non-AI items from the Academic Integrity Guide (coder A). Document stance was delegates for all five documents in both codings.
